outcome: Adverse perinatal outcomes (perinatal mortality up to 7 days, low Apgar score at 5 min, asphyxia, neonatal intensive care unit admission >=24 h)
cohort: The study included 143,146 women in their second pregnancy with one previous cesarean birth, no prior vaginal birth, who gave birth to a term singleton in cephalic presentation in the Netherlands between 2000 and 2019.
finding: The proportion of women intending VBAC after one previous cesarean birth in the Netherlands significantly decreased from 2000 to 2019, a decline not accompanied by a synchronous reduction in perinatal mortality, despite adverse outcomes being higher in the intended VBAC group.
mod_finding: The rate of intended VBAC decreased by 21.5% (from 77.2% to 55.7%) and its success rate dropped from 71.0% to 65.3% over 20 years, resulting in an increase in the overall cesarean birth rate from 45.2% to 63.6%, with adverse perinatal outcomes higher in the intended VBAC group compared to the planned cesarean birth group.
